singular-registry-economics-as-decided.text: Decided on 13 October 2026, after the review of the first draft of the economics paper; the operator ruled each point of the review. This page is the design the Lean model states and the paper explains. It replaces the earlier design, with its bond, processor split, booking root and termination fee.

story.text: As a requester, I book a registration knowing what it costs:
If it succeeds, I pay the registration cost to the treasury and the tip to whoever processes it.
If it fails, I get everything back except the tip.
If I cancel it in the reclaim window, I get everything back, the tip included.
Nobody can cancel my live request. Nobody can make a termination fail once it is booked.
As a reviewer, I can check every claim against a Lean theorem. Where the paper makes no promise (spam, delay, priority, fee changes), it says so.

what-changed-from-the-first-draft.text: What changed from the first draft.

Terminology (operator): Singular has no controller concept. The application is the controller. It authorizes every operation through its application tag and governs the singular tag at the destination it names. A registration request carries a refund address, its owner field.

registry-parameters-all-fixed-at-creatio.text: Registry parameters (all fixed at creation; no authority can change them).

The paper states the envelope each parameter was sized for: ledger fee parameters, inclusion delay and output minimums at creation. Outside it, a pending request may wait without bound, and new bookings may offer more than t_min. The answer to a changed ledger is a new registry, and nothing migrates to it.

the-two-requests.text: The request policy, the minting policy that mints a booked request's syntax tag, refuses any request whose contents are not exactly the following ("dirty requests").
How a termination is booked: the key's token lives at the destination its registration named, under the application's custody. The application's rule releases it into a termination request:
cardano-keri releases it on a verified duplicity proof, which anyone may post;
open-datum releases it on its envelope's control signature.

Singular checks the application tag, not the application's rule. Everything the fold checks for a termination is fixed at booking. Both tag policies allow a burn at any time with no further condition, for both kinds of request. A rejection by anyone must be able to burn the application tag, and a booked termination, which has no other exit, must not be stranded.

the-tags.text: The syntax tag is minted when a request is booked and burned when that request is spent, by any exit: fold, retraction or rejection. There is no syntax tag without a pending request and no pending request without its syntax tag.

The application tag has the same life. It is minted at booking and burned by every exit. The syntax tag authorizes the request's shape and the application tag authorizes the operation. The application tag is never returned to anyone.
The singular tag is minted at the destination by a registration fold and burned by the termination fold.
registration fold: burns the syntax tag and the application tag, and mints the singular tag at the destination;
termination fold: burns the syntax tag, the singular tag and the application tag;
rejection and retraction: burn the syntax tag and the application tag.
The supply of each tag equals the count of pending requests.

Burning is free: the tag policies allow a burn with no condition. This is safe because a tag exists only in a request output at the Singular script hash, and that output can be spent only through the request validator, which enforces the exit and requires the request's tags to be burned in the same transaction, so that no exit carries a live tag out. The exit rules belong to the request validator's spend, not to the burn branch of a tag policy.

An output at the request address that lacks either tag is not a request, because a syntax tag is minted only together with an application tag. Anyone may spend it. A tagged output leaves only through one of its exits.

every-exit.text: A registration's windows, measured from its booked time s:
Every exit burns the syntax tag and the application tag; the termination fold also burns the singular tag.
A fold of n registrations and m terminations donates at least n·R plus the sum, over the m terminations, of (held − tip).

the-rejection-rule.text: A rejection reads the registry state output as a reference input. It checks that the referenced output carries this registry's exact state token (policy and name) and reads the root from that output's datum.
It spends only the requests it rejects, and burns each rejected request's syntax tag and application tag. It spends no state token, and this is checked.
Rejection is removed from the fold's action list entirely. Only folds spend the state output.
Rejections batch: one transaction may reject many requests against one referenced state output, with one shared validity interval.
Each request is consumed and refunded once.
Refunds are summed per refund address.
Evidence is checked for every member.
A fold that lands first invalidates the rejections in flight. They are rebuilt; this starvation is accepted. A rejection that loses the race is invalid and pays no fee.
a current lifecycle mismatch, against the referenced state;
expiry, at or after s + W_p + W_r.
A live registration that can still be folded is never rejected. A termination is never rejected.

what-the-paper-may-state.text: Each statement becomes a result only once its definitions and proofs exist in Lean. Until then the paper marks it as pending.
Every fold preserves every registry parameter. Today's preservation (onlyRootChanged in Model.lean), extended to R, t_min and δ.

No accepted rejection or rejection batch spends the registry state output or changes the registry (map, token supply). This must hold for every accepted transaction, not just for what the builder produces.
A rejection ordered before a fold cannot invalidate that fold through the state output. Whole-fold validity also needs disjoint other inputs.

A registration that can still be folded is not rejected before expiry. This is today's live_compatible_request_protected (Statements.lean), lifted to the reference-read rejection. With the booked-time rule, expiry comes no earlier than W_p + W_r after the booking's actual inclusion.
No rejection without current-state evidence: today's rejection_without_evidence.
on rejection, each refund address receives at least the sum, over its distinct rejected requests, of (held − tip) in lovelace;
on retraction, it receives everything the request held except the two tags, which are burned.
Registration charge: every accepted fold that registers n keys donates at least n·R. R is returned on rejection and retraction, and never after a successful registration.
Terminations are unrejectable: in every reachable state, no rejection of a termination request carrying its key's genuine token is admitted, on either ground.
The mismatch half follows from biconditional_supply_sync (Statements.lean) once the token held in a pending request is counted in supply.
The expiry half holds by definition, since a termination has no expiry.
At most one termination per key is pending. This follows from token uniqueness across custody and pending requests (active_witness_unique, Statements.lean, extended).
Only terminations carrying the application tag fold.
A booked termination can be folded at any later time. This holds as long as some folder accepts its tip and ledger fees stay inside the envelope the tip was sized for.
Across a batch, what the processors can take is at most the sum of the tips. This needs a balance relation with no outside funding.
t_min covers the measured cost of every supported exit processed alone, refund output included, within the stated fee envelope. This is conditional on the measurements.

what-the-paper-must-not-claim.text: What the paper must not claim.
A flood price, or any spam deterrence beyond the spent R. Valid folds of junk keys still take turns on the state output; R mitigates this and does not prevent it.
That nothing delays a fold, that malicious folds are excluded, or that any request is included, prioritized or served within a bound.
An exact or always-positive processor wage. An optimal value of R, t_min or δ.
That the parameters stay sufficient after the ledger's fee parameters or output minimums change.
Key ownership, squatting protection, or any cardano-keri guarantee as a property of Singular. Those belong to the application.
That the deployed validators implement any of this, without conformance evidence.

lean-additions-in-dependency-order.text: Lean additions, in dependency order.
Transaction vocabulary.
Output references and their presence in the current UTxO set, so that "a reference to a spent output is refused" can be stated.
Reference inputs alongside spending inputs.
The exact state token identity (policy and name).
Actual input and output values, with native assets.
The donation field (a zero amount omits it), the ledger fee, and a balance relation scoped to these transactions.
Parameters R, t_min and δ, with preservation.
Request types.
A registration carries the refund address, the destination, s, R, the tip and the carrier ada.
A termination carries the singular tag, the tip and the carrier ada, with no refund address and no time.
Both carry the application tag and the syntax tag, with its provenance.
The exact-contents predicate, with the declared tip separated from the held value.
Booking transitions.
Registration booking: the validity interval no wider than δ, and s = U.
Termination booking: the token moves from application custody into the request.
The supply invariant spans custody and pending requests until the burn.
Rejection.
The reference-read rejection batch: state-token check, no state spend, distinct inputs, one interval, per-member admission.
Refunds of held − tip, summed per refund address.
The rejection arm is removed from the fold.
Terminations are excluded by construction (no expiry) and by theorem (mismatch is impossible).
Fold.
The processing window for registrations and no window for terminations; today's on-chain gate applies to both, and the termination must lose it.
Routing of R, the tip and the carrier.
Termination burns the singular tag and the application tag and donates held − tip.
The donation is at least n·R plus the terminations' donations.
Theorems 1–13, with negative controls:
the old state-spending rejection path;
a fake, foreign or stale referenced state;
an overlapping state spend;
a live member inside a rejection batch;
a repeated input or a reused refund;
a dirty request, or hidden surplus;
a forged syntax tag, singular tag or application tag;
a backdated booking or one wider than δ;
a termination stranded by a check made at fold time;
one donation counted for many keys.
Correspondence, to be done separately:
validators and conformance rows;
measured fees, output minimums and batch capacity.

open-items-not-decided.text: The fate of a registration's application tag on a successful fold is decided: it is burned, never returned, so no restitution output exists and t_min covers none.

Adapting open-datum (applications/open-datum). Today it releases the token inside the terminating fold and pays the deposit to its control signer. The decision moves the release to booking, and the deposit payment must be reconciled with the treasury donation. Its application tag policy must allow a burn at any time, for both kinds of request.

Adapting cardano-keri. Its model reaps the token, then refunds a go-request to the reaper and pays the convictor a reward. That differs from the decided termination, so a correspondence design is needed.
Values: R, t_min, δ and the carrier minimum, measured on the target network and chosen per registry.

The relation between the existing fee pin (maxFee) and the minimum tip t_min: both are pinned and checked, and no statement assumes how they relate. It is settled when the validators are made to agree with the model.

The source of the carrier amount: slice six of the Lean model checks the held value against a carrier allocation the requester declares and makes no claim that it equals the ledger's minimum; whether the amount stays declared or is pinned by the registry is not decided.
